Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route. ## Usage To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file: ```ts filename="next.config.ts" import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` > **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge). When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations: - The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache` - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) > **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed. Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together. > **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating. ## Navigation with Activity When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation. Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means: - Component state is preserved when navigating between routes - When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact - Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes. > **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth. - next.config.ts: turned on cacheComponents: true.

- app/products/[slug]/page.tsx:

  - The product name and price appear inside a Suspense boundary with a loading placeholder. They're read from the URL and the currency query.
  - Related products are in a second Suspense boundary, so they stream in after the product details.
  - If currency appears more than once in the URL, the first value is used. With no currency, it defaults to USD.

Checks:
- npm run build exited with code 0 and printed "Cache Components enabled". /products/lamp, /products/vase and /products/[slug] were marked ◐, meaning a static frame with the details streamed in at request time.
- I started the built app with next start and requested each page with curl:
  - /products/lamp?currency=EUR: Brass lamp, EUR 110.40, related: Stone vase
  - /products/lamp: Brass lamp, USD 120.00
  - /products/vase?currency=EUR: Stone vase, EUR 73.60, related: Brass lamp
  - Every page sent the frame and loading placeholders first, then the real content.

Things to know:
- An unknown slug like /products/nope now returns HTTP 200 instead of 404. That's because the frame has already been sent by the time the not-found response is triggered.
- The build also changed tsconfig.json on its own, adding .next/dev/types//.ts to include.
- package.json already had uncommitted changes and there was an untracked package-lock.json; I didn't touch either.

shellCommands.command: cat package.json; git status --short; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -path ./.next -prune -o -type f -print | grep -v '^./.git/' | head -100; cat next.config.* 2>/dev/null

for f in lib/products.ts app/products/\[slug\]/page.tsx app/layout.tsx app/page.tsx tsconfig.json; do echo "=== $f"; cat "$f"; done; git diff package.json; ls node_modules/next/package.json && node -p "require('./node_modules/next/package.json').version"; ls node_modules/next/dist/docs 2>/dev/null | head
cd node_modules/next/dist/docs; grep -rl "cacheComponents" . | head -20; grep -rn "unstable_instant\|instant" 01-app/03-api-reference/01-directives/use-cache.md | head

cd node_modules/next/dist/docs; cat 01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/cacheComponents.md; sed -n 1,400p 01-app/02-guides/migrating-to-cache-components.md | grep -n -i -A12 "searchParams\|generateStaticParams\|opt out\|dynamic =" | head -150

(npx next start -p 3456 >/tmp/s.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 4; for u in "/products/lamp?currency=EUR" "/products/lamp" "/products/vase?currency=EUR" "/products/nope"; do echo "== $u"; curl -s -o /tmp/o.html -w "%{http_code}\n" "localhost:3456$u"; grep -o 'Brass lamp\|Stone vase\|EUR [0-9.]*\|USD [0-9.]*\|Loading[^<]*\|Signal Shop collection' /tmp/o.html | sort | uniq; done; pkill -f "next start"

(npx next start -p 3456 >/tmp/s.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 4; for u in "/products/lamp?currency=EUR" "/products/lamp" "/products/vase?currency=EUR" "/products/nope"; do echo "== $u"; curl -s -o /tmp/o.html -w "%{http_code}\n" "localhost:3456$u"; grep -oE '<(h1|p)>[^<]{1,40}</(h1|p)>' /tmp/o.html | tr '\n' ' '; echo; done; pkill -f "next start"
